Walmart officially announced this morning that it will finally begin rolling out Apple Pay, ending its refusal of over a decade.

When will Apple Pay be available at your Walmart? I have the complete rollout timeline, with all the details here…

Walmart Apple Pay rollout timeline

In a statement today, Walmart said Apple Pay and broader contactless payment support will begin rolling out as soon as next week, and will cover all stores nationwide by the end of this year.

9to5Mac has obtained the internal memo Walmart sent to its store managers today, which provides more detailed rollout specifics. The company is currently planning a phased, state-by-state rollout. If any issues arise during the process, dates may be adjusted, and here is the current roadmap:

States Tap to Pay Launch Arkansas Aug. 24–31 California, Washington, Oregon, Nevada, Idaho, Alaska, Hawaii Sept. 10 Kansas, Louisiana, Nebraska, Oklahoma Sept. 14 Texas Sept. 17 Arizona, Utah, Colorado, New Mexico, South Dakota, Montana, North Dakota, Wyoming Sept. 21 Illinois, Ohio, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Iowa Sept. 24 Tennessee, Indiana, Michigan, Kentucky Sept. 28 Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi Oct. 1 Florida Oct. 5 North Carolina, Virginia, South Carolina, West Virginia, Puerto Rico Oct. 8 Pennsylvania, New York, New Jersey, Massachusetts, Maryland, Connecticut, New Hampshire, Maine, Delaware, Rhode Island, Vermont, District of Columbia Oct. 12

The current timeline appears to be missing Missouri, for reasons unknown.

Walmart also listed in its internal memo all the contactless payment methods that will be supported:

  • Contactless-enabled credit and debit cards
  • Digital wallets, including Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Samsung Pay
  • Payment-enabled smartwatches and wearables
  • Contactless-enabled EBT cards

Walmart is long overdue for supporting Apple Pay. Will this change where you choose to shop? Let us know in the comments.
